ayahOccurrences.text: يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓ ۚ أَيُمْسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓ ۚ أَيُمْسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: يَدُسُّهُۥ is in the derivative form: يَدُسُّ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
د/س/س   d–s–s to shove in, to infiltrate, to hide in, to adulterate, to bury; a spy, a plot, intrigue; sand adder. Of this root, يَدُسُّ yaduss occurs 11 times in the Qur’an. (Qur’anic word دَسَّاهَا dassāhā is not considered here, as it is viewed by a number of philologists as an elongated form of دَسّىَ dassā)
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
يَدُسُّ yaduss [imperf. of v. دَسَّ dassa, trans.] to bury, to shove in

(16:59) أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَى هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِى التُّرَابِ should he keep it [the newborn girl] in humiliation (or, and suffer humiliation himself) or bury her in the dust?
